title: A run on a different numeric backend is a different run
note: scientific.run_identity's environment record: the CPU's SIMD set and core, the thread and dispatch variables, and the native build read from each wheel's RECORD -- each shown to change the RunIdentity and make may_reuse refuse, while mitigation flags and unrelated variables do not; read without importing numpy.

mutations.name: RB1_simd_features_unrecorded
mutations.rationale: a CPU with another SIMD set dispatches another kernel and looks the same

mutations.name: RB2_the_core_unrecorded
mutations.rationale: a BLAS picking kernels for another core looks the same

mutations.name: RB3_every_flag_counts
mutations.find: flags |= {f for f in value.split() if _SIMD_FLAG.match(f)}
mutations.rationale: a microcode mitigation makes every patched host a different machine

mutations.name: RB4_thread_and_dispatch_variables_unrecorded
mutations.rationale: a thread count or a dispatch override changes the digits and not the identity

mutations.name: RB5_the_native_build_unrecorded
mutations.rationale: another native build of the same version is the same run

mutations.name: RB6_native_hashes_ignored
mutations.rationale: the native digest names the files and not what they contain

mutations.name: RB7_an_unreadable_cpu_is_any_cpu
mutations.rationale: two machines whose CPUs cannot be read reuse each other's runs

mutations.name: RB8_only_this_process_environment
mutations.find: environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
mutations.rationale: the record describes the caller, not the tool that ran

mutations.name: RB9_the_cpu_is_always_this_one
mutations.find:
"cpu": cpu_record(_read_cpuinfo() if cpuinfo is _READ
                              else cpuinfo),
mutations.rationale: the record cannot describe any CPU but the one it runs on
